bull_bear.body:
- Economies of scale in chlor-alkali manufacturing
- State of the art eco-friendly technologies, including imported ThyssenKrupp membrane cell electrolysers progressively upgraded to latest-generation cell elements
- Extensive usage of renewable energy, with 590 million units of renewable power consumed in FY 2025-26 amounting to 35.7% of total power consumption
- Integrated downstream plants enabling captive chlorine consumption
- Strong network for marketing and distribution
- In-house Research and Development facilities, with collaborative programmes with BITS Pilani Goa Campus, CSMCRI and NACL Industries Limited
- Proximity to major raw material sources and markets
- EcoVadis assessment score of 71/100, placing the Company in the 87th percentile with a Silver Medal rating
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Power cost and grid dependence in a power-intensive process — The Company describes its operations as power intensive. Higher fuel cost (natural gas and coal) and major dependence on grid power sourced from DISCOMs make availability of economic power supply a major area of concern, which management is addressing by adding further renewable power to the energy mix.
- New caustic soda capacity being added by large competitors — Management explicitly flags a potential business risk from the proposed addition of large new Caustic Soda capacity by two big Indian business houses. Mitigation steps already started include optimising chlorine integration for a better operating rate, increasing exports of solid caustic soda products and developing new usages for caustic soda.
- Product concentration in the Caustic Soda group — The major portion of the Company's revenue comes from Caustic Soda group products and the business operates under a single segment, Chemical Manufacturing, so the caustic soda and chlorine market scenario has a wide impact on performance and amplifies the effect of any caustic soda oversupply or price weakness.
- Chlor-alkali price cycle and demand softness — Throughout FY 2025-26 the prices of chlor-alkali products were under pressure due to various geographical issues as well as moderate demand from all the key segments, although the caustic soda segment recovered towards the year end.
- Currency and refinancing exposure on borrowings — The Company availed External Commercial Borrowing of USD 68.70 Million to part finance expansion, and made a pre-payment of USD 34.35 Million along with a half yearly installment of USD 6.87 Million due to high currency fluctuations. It availed a term loan from HDFC Bank to repay the ECB, secured against the assets of the CLM plant at Dahej, repayable in five half yearly installments with the last repayment on 17th March 2028.
- Competition-law litigation with the Delhi Jal Board — A Competition Commission of India investigation into alleged contravention of Section 3(1) read with 3(3)(d) of the Competition Act, 2002 in respect of sales of chemical products to the Delhi Jal Board resulted in a penalty order which the Company has appealed before the NCLAT. The NCLAT granted a stay subject to a deposit of 10% of the penalty amount, and the matter is at the stage of final arguments.
- Project execution risk across a large concurrent expansion slate — Several projects are under implementation at once, including the Chlorotoluene Downstream Plant, the Caustic Soda Flaking Plant, the HCl Synthesis Unit and the Cell Element Replacement Project, all targeted for commissioning during FY 2026-27, alongside multiple renewable SPVs. The Hydrazine Hydrate Plant remains under a stabilization phase with production levels still being improved gradually.
- Dependence on renewable SPV partners and their commissioning timelines — A material part of the planned power-cost reduction depends on third-party SPVs with Aditya Birla Renewable Energy, Clean Max and GIPCL, plus short and medium-term solar purchase arrangements, so delayed commissioning of any of these projects would delay the cost benefit.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: GACL operates in a single segment, Chemical Manufacturing, producing caustic soda and chlorine-chain derivatives together with phosphoric acid, hydrogen peroxide, caustic potash and specialty chemicals from complexes at Vadodara and Dahej in Gujarat. The business is built around integrated downstream plants that consume chlorine captively, backed by state-of-the-art membrane-cell electrolysis technology and a large renewable power portfolio. Products are sold into domestic industrial markets and exported, with the Company reporting its highest-ever exports during FY 2025-26.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Chemical Manufacturing:** Caustic Soda (lye and solid/flakes), Chlorine, Caustic Potash / Potassium Hydroxide (KOH), Hydrochloric Acid, Hydrogen Peroxide, Phosphoric Acid (Purified and Food Grade), Hydrazine Hydrate, Chlorotoluenes, Benzyl Chloride, Benzyl Alcohol, Benzaldehyde
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- GACL-NALCO Alkalies and Chemicals Private Limited (GNAL) — subsidiary: 60% held by GACL; joint venture with National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO), which holds 40%. Operates a caustic soda plant and captive power plant at Dahej, Gujarat. Became a material subsidiary effective 1st April 2024; participates in the Company's Business Responsibility initiatives. The Managing Director of GACL is Chairperson of GNAL and draws no remuneration or sitting fees from it.

- Aditya Birla Renewables SPV 4 Limited — associate: SPV formed for a 62.7 MW renewable hybrid power project in Gujarat for captive power use by the Company; GACL holds 26%; a GACL officer serves as Nominee Director on its board. Classified as a Joint Venture in the BRSR holding/subsidiary/associate table and as an Associate in the related-party note.
- Clean Max Sphere Energy Private Limited — associate: SPV formed for a 75.9 MW renewable hybrid power project in Gujarat for captive power use by the Company; GACL acquired a 26% stake on 18.10.2025

- Economies of scale in chlor-alkali manufacturing

- Extensive usage of renewable energy, with 590 million units of renewable power consumed in FY 2025-26 amounting to 35.7% of total power consumption
- Integrated downstream plants enabling captive chlorine consumption
- Strong network for marketing and distribution

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Optimise power cost, which is the dominant cost lever for a power-intensive chlor-alkali business, by raising the share of renewable energy in the mix through group-captive and SPV structures with GIPCL, Aditya Birla Renewables and Clean Max Sphere Energy, plus short/medium-term solar purchases from NVVNL, Tata Power, Kreate Energy and P R Energy
- Upgrade old-generation electrolysers to the latest-generation membrane cell technology (4th generation to 6th generation B+ elements, and a placed order to replace 590 old 4B cell elements with energy-efficient 6B+ elements) to lower specific power consumption and manufacturing cost
- Strengthen downstream integration and captive chlorine consumption through the chlorotoluenes chain, with the Chlorotoluene Downstream Project under implementation
- Convert caustic soda from liquid to solid form via a latest-technology Flaker Unit with a view to enhancing export potential
- Grow exports as a structural channel, having achieved ever-highest exports of Rs.946 Crores standalone and Rs.1242 Crores including GNAL
- Drive R&D-led import substitution and alternate sourcing for critical raw materials such as rock phosphate and amyl alcohol, alongside development of value-added products (dibenzyl ether, MKP, DKP, TKP, benzyl acetate, sodium benzoate, benzyl salicylate) that have reached pilot scale
- Pursue collaborative research with BITS Pilani Goa Campus, CSMCRI and NACL Industries Limited focused on waste utilization, sustainable technologies and value-added products
- Expand renewable capacity further, including an MOU signed with GMDC to explore additional renewable assets in SPV mode, and continuing discussions with RE developers to tie up further RE projects
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: GACL is pursuing a structured growth strategy focused on portfolio diversification, value addition to its chlorine chain, higher captive chlorine consumption and operational flexibility. The 30 KTPA Chlorotoluenes Plant at Dahej, described as India's largest integrated facility for Benzyl Chloride, Benzyl Alcohol and Benzaldehyde, ramped up significantly during FY 2025-26 to approximately 80% capacity utilisation and is expected to run at full capacity in FY 2026-27; the Hydrazine Hydrate Plant remains under stabilisation. A 40 TPD Chlorotoluenes Downstream Project is being implemented at Dahej for 2 downstream products in phase-I, the third product originally envisaged having been dropped. A 200 TPD Caustic Soda Flaking Unit and a 120 TPD Hydrochloric Acid Synthesis Unit are being installed and are expected to be commissioned by the end of FY 2026-27, alongside investments in a new boiler facility and replacement of selected electrolyser cell elements with next-generation energy-efficient cell technology (an order was placed for 590 old 4B elements to be replaced with 6B+ elements, imported via Thyssenkrupp Nucera India). Building on the existing Food Grade Phosphoric Acid facility, an additional 33,870 TPA Food Grade Phosphoric Acid plant is planned at Dahej. Caustic Potash capacity at Vadodara is being enhanced by converting existing caustic soda cells, with electrolyser reallocation raising Potassium Hydroxide capacity from 120 TPD to 200 TPD. A 5,000 TPA High Purity / Electronic Grade Hydrogen Peroxide facility is being set up to serve semiconductor, electronics and high-purity chemical demand. During FY 2026-27 the Company plans to commission the HCl Synthesis Unit, Chlorotoluene Downstream Plant, Caustic Soda Flaking Plant and Cell Element Replacement Project. On power, a 75 MW Group Captive Solar Power Plant with GIPCL and GSFC was commissioned in two phases (25 MW in April 2025 and 50 MW in June 2025), with GACL holding a 37.5 MW (50%) share; a 62.7 MW hybrid SPV with Aditya Birla Renewable Energy is expected operational by around October 2026 / Q2 FY 2026-27; and a 75.9 MW hybrid SPV with Clean Max is phased with 16.5 MW by October 2026 and 59.4 MW by March 2027. The Company is further evaluating proposals for up to 100 MW (minimum 40 MW) of hybrid renewable power under the SPV model with agreements expected to be finalised in Q2 FY 2026-27, and has signed an MOU with GMDC to explore additional renewable assets in SPV mode.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Power cost is the principal margin lever: the Company describes its operations as power intensive and reports that a higher share of cheaper renewable energy reduced the weighted average power cost during the year
- Renewable power consumption reached 590 million units in FY 2025-26, representing 35.7% of total power consumption at GACL as a whole, with further group-captive and SPV hybrid projects being commissioned through FY 2026-27
- Energy-efficiency capex is expected to compound: the Company invested Rs. 10,350 Lakhs towards energy conservation initiatives and equipment, with estimated savings of Rs. 2,686.17 Lakhs achieved at Dahej Complex-I during FY 2025-26, and states further savings would be achieved during current and subsequent financial years
- Upgradation of Electrolyzer IJKL elements from 4th to 6th Generation (B+) at the Caustic Soda Plant is estimated to save 327.25 lakh kWh per annum, corresponding to a reduction in specific energy consumption of approximately 340 kWh per MT of Caustic Soda Production
- Exports are a growing demand channel, with the Company describing a quantum leap in export capabilities and record export turnover
- GNAL, the 60%-held joint venture at Dahej, has completed start-up of all its units including both units of the 130 MW Power Plant, with the Caustic Soda Plant, Flaking Unit and Power Plant consistently operating at higher capacity during 2025-26
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

The Company has undertaken installation of a latest technology Flaker Unit for conversion of Caustic Soda from liquid to solid form with a view to enhancing its export potential, with technology from Bertrams Chemical Plants, Switzerland and implementation under progress.

Higher fuel cost (natural gas and coal) and major dependence on grid power sourced from DISCOMs make availability of economic power supply a major area of concern; the Company is adding further renewable power to the energy mix to overcome this.

Management flags a potential business risk from the proposed addition of large new Caustic Soda capacity by two big Indian business houses, and is mitigating through chlorine integration, higher exports of solid caustic soda and new caustic soda usages.

The Company placed an order for replacement of 590 old generation 4B Cell Elements with energy-efficient 6B+ new generation Cell Elements, imported through Thyssenkrupp Nucera India Private Limited, with implementation under progress.

Project Ahvaan, the flagship transformation programme run with A.T. Kearney across procurement, manufacturing, commercial operations, supply chain and energy management, generated an estimated annualized value creation potential of approximately Rs. 100 Crore during FY 2025-26, with initiatives at various stages of implementation.

Reallocation of electrolysers at the Vadodara complex will increase Potassium Hydroxide (KOH) production capacity from 120 TPD to 200 TPD, through conversion of existing caustic soda manufacturing cells.

sk.overview: India's industrial catalyst and adsorbent ecosystem plays a critical role in enabling efficient, sustainable, and high-quality production across refining, petrochemical, chemical, fertilizer, and gas-processing industries.
